correctness.rationale: The four-case partition by placement of label 2 is exhaustive and disjoint. In the two-sided case the unique earliest B-class with a 2 and latest A-class with a 2 exactly determine which canonical classes may contain 0 and which may contain 2; the boundary classes must contain a 2. Multiplying the resulting class enumerators therefore counts each Roman dominating function exactly once. A standard-library brute-force checker independently matched every coefficient for all 255 positive canonical chain profiles through order 9, totaling 3,023,307 assignments and 4,351 coefficient comparisons. The finite check corroborates, but does not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The originality-bearing statement is the complete all-weight Roman-domination classification and product formula for arbitrary connected chain graphs. The published complete-bipartite formula is explicitly treated as prior coverage. Full-text inspection of the 2021 polynomial paper and the 2023 Roman Census paper found no implication of the general chain formula; the former covers complete bipartite graphs and other operations, while the latter enumerates minimal functions on other graph classes. Targeted semantic searches returned no stronger chain/Ferrers all-weight result. The directly relevant 2020 chain-graph minimum-optimization paper could not be fully inspected, so possible incidental stronger coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of doi:10.1007/s12190-020-01345-4 was not lawfully accessible during review; although accessible metadata frames it as minimum-weight optimization, an incidental all-function formula cannot be ruled out from metadata alone.
Poorly indexed older literature may use Ferrers, difference, or nested bipartite terminology without the phrase chain graph.

Failed semantic searches are not themselves novelty proofs; PASS rests on statement-level comparison with the inspected primary literature plus the absence of stronger coverage in the checked records.

value.rationale: The Roman domination polynomial is a named enumerative invariant, and chain graphs are a natural structured family already studied for Roman minimum optimization. The theorem gives the entire weight distribution for every connected chain graph from canonical twin-class data, strictly more information than the minimum value and extending the known complete-bipartite boundary case. The nested-threshold classification is reusable structural information rather than a small numerical increment or arbitrary slice.
